source: Built-in example; default title and axes; both views

cumulative.plain: This analysis combined 9 studies. The pooled effect on the supplied analysis scale was −0.290 (95% confidence interval −0.385 to −0.195). The confidence interval does not include zero on this scale. The prediction interval for a similar new study was −0.521 to −0.059. This summary does not establish causation or clinical importance.
cumulative.methods: Estimates were pooled on the supplied scale with inverse-variance random-effects weights. Paule–Mandel estimated the between-study variance (τ²; Paule and Mandel 1982). Within-study variances were squared standard errors. No transformation, back-transformation or continuity correction was applied by the app. The pooled 95% confidence interval used a normal Wald approximation without Hartung–Knapp adjustment. Prediction intervals used the pooled estimate ± t × √(τ² + SE²), with t degrees of freedom equal to the number of studies minus one, computed whenever at least two studies were pooled (Cochrane Handbook v6.5, §10.10.4.3). Each cumulative prefix was refitted, ordered by ascending year with ties retaining input order. No pooled-effect p-value or overall study-level I² is reported by this app. Analyses were run in allmeta cumulative-subgroup <build.version> (commit <build.shortSha>).
cumulative.results: The final cumulative pooled effect across 9 studies was −0.290 (95% CI −0.385 to −0.195); τ² = 0.0077. The 95% prediction interval was −0.521 to −0.059.
flags: Tests for small-study effects would be underpowered; none were performed.
references: Paule RC, Mandel J. Consensus values and weighting factors. J Res Natl Bur Stand 1982;87:377-385.
Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions, version 6.5, section 10.10.4.3 (Prediction intervals in random-effects meta-analysis).

subgroup.plain: This analysis combined 9 studies. The pooled effect on the supplied analysis scale was −0.290 (95% confidence interval −0.385 to −0.195). The confidence interval does not include zero on this scale. The prediction interval for a similar new study was −0.521 to −0.059. This summary does not establish causation or clinical importance.
subgroup.methods: Estimates were pooled on the supplied scale with inverse-variance random-effects weights. Paule–Mandel estimated the between-study variance (τ²; Paule and Mandel 1982). Within-study variances were squared standard errors. No transformation, back-transformation or continuity correction was applied by the app. The pooled 95% confidence interval used a normal Wald approximation without Hartung–Knapp adjustment. Prediction intervals used the pooled estimate ± t × √(τ² + SE²), with t degrees of freedom equal to the number of studies minus one, computed whenever at least two studies were pooled (Cochrane Handbook v6.5, §10.10.4.3). Subgroups with more than one study had a separately estimated τ²; missing group labels were retained as an ungrouped category. The overall estimate pooled all studies separately. Between-subgroup Q used inverse squared subgroup pooled standard errors as weights, centred on the weighted mean of subgroup estimates. Its p-value used a chi-squared distribution with the number of groups minus one degrees of freedom. I² of subgroup differences was the nonnegative percentage (Q − df)/Q; it is not overall study-level I². No pooled-effect p-value or overall study-level I² is reported by this app. Analyses were run in allmeta cumulative-subgroup <build.version> (commit <build.shortSha>).
subgroup.results: The overall pooled effect across 9 studies was −0.290 (95% CI −0.385 to −0.195); τ² = 0.0077. The 95% prediction interval was −0.521 to −0.059. There were 2 subgroups. Between-subgroup Q = 9.76 (df = 1); p = 0.002; I² of differences = 89.7%. Subgroups are listed in the plot’s order. Subgroup 1: 4 studies; pooled effect −0.444 (CI −0.574 to −0.313); τ² = 0.0000; prediction interval −0.656 to −0.232. Subgroup 2: 5 studies; pooled effect −0.193 (CI −0.281 to −0.105); τ² = 0.0000; prediction interval −0.317 to −0.069.
flags: Tests for small-study effects would be underpowered; none were performed.
At least one subgroup has few studies: heterogeneity estimates are imprecise.
Subgroup comparisons are observational and do not establish effect modification.
references: Paule RC, Mandel J. Consensus values and weighting factors. J Res Natl Bur Stand 1982;87:377-385.
Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions, version 6.5, section 10.10.4.3 (Prediction intervals in random-effects meta-analysis).
